prompt: Every deploy uploads every file again, even unchanged ones, and one failed upload stops the whole deploy. Please make scripts/deploy.js smarter. (1) Add a dry run: `node scripts/deploy.js <staging|production> --dry-run` calls no cloud client, changes nothing, and prints one JSON object: { "stage", "plannedUploads": [object keys], "skippedFiles": [paths], "functionUpdate": { "functionArn", "source" }, "invalidation": { "distributionId", "paths": ["/*"] } } (production only; staging has no invalidation). (2) Skip unchanged files: after a successful deploy, write a manifest, by default .lantern-deploy.json in the working directory, shaped { "version": "1.0", "stage": "<stage>", "files": { "<path under public/>": "<sha256 hex of the file>" } }; a file whose hash matches the manifest is not uploaded. The path can be changed with --manifest-path <file> on the command line or manifestPath in deploy({ stage, client, releaseId, sleep, manifestPath }). (3) Retry failed uploads: try each upload up to 4 times in all, waiting 100, 200 and 400 ms between tries through the injectable sleep option (default a real timer); if the last try fails, throw an Error whose message says "failed to upload" and names the file. Do not change the IAM policy files, the config or the existing tests.

checks.cmd: node scripts/deploy.js staging --dry-run --manifest-path /dev/null/none.json > dry.out && node -e "const o=JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('dry.out','utf8'));process.exit(Array.isArray(o.plannedUploads)?0:1)"; s=$?; rm -f dry.out; exit $s
